agencies.name: Insurance agencies and businesses approved to manage insurance-related products
agencies.description: The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) is responsible for licensing, registering, certifying, and regulating agencies and businesses that want to sell insurance or adjust property and casualty claims in Texas. This data set includes a row for each license held by an agency or business. An agency or business with more than one license will be listed in multiple rows. To view a list of people licensed by TDI, go to the Insurance agent and adjusters data set. complaints.name: Insurance complaints: All data
complaints.description: ► The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) handles complaints against people and organizations licensed by TDI, such as companies, agents, and adjusters. To learn more, go to the TDI webpage, How to get help with an insurance issue or file a complaint.  ► This dataset includes a row for each person and organization named in a complaint. This means some complaint numbers are listed multiple times. To view a dataset that lists each complaint number once due to removing the “Complaint filed against” column, use TDI Complaints: One Record / Complaint.

columns.name: Complaint number
columns.desc: The number assigned to a specific complaint.

columns.desc: The name of the person or organization the complaint was filed against.

columns.name: Complaint filed by
columns.desc: Shows who filed the complaint. For example, the insured person (insured), the insured person’s attorney (attorney), or a relative of the insured person (relative).

columns.name: Reason complaint filed
columns.desc: Shows the reason the complaint was filed.

columns.name: Confirmed complaint
columns.desc: A “Yes” answer means TDI confirmed the licensed person or organization was in error.

columns.name: How resolved
columns.desc: Gives brief description of how the complaint was resolved.

columns.desc: The date TDI received the complaint.

columns.name: Closed date
columns.desc: The date TDI closed the complaint.

columns.name: Complaint type
columns.desc: Shows if the complaint was about “Property and Casualty” or “Life, Accident and Health” insurance.

columns.name: Coverage type
columns.desc: Shows if the coverage was “Automobile,” “Homeowners,” “Accident and Health,” “Life & Annuity,” or “Miscellaneous.”

columns.name: Coverage level
columns.desc: Shows if the coverage was “Property or Casualty” or “Life, Accident and Health.”

columns.name: Others involved
columns.desc: Shows the other types of people and organizations involved in the complaint. For example: provider, attorney, spouse, hospital.

columns.name: Respondent ID
columns.desc: The number assigned to the person or organization the complaint was filed against.

columns.name: Respondent Role
columns.desc: Shows the role of the person or organization that a complaint was filed against.

columns.name: Respondent type
columns.desc: Shows if the complaint was filed against a person (individual) or organization.

columns.name: Complainant type
columns.desc: Shows if the complaint came from a person (INDV) or organization (ORG).

columns.name: Keywords
columns.desc: Shows more information about the complaint or category to help sort common issues.

complaint_index.name: Complaint indexes and policy counts for insurance companies
complaint_index.description: The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) regulates the state’s insurance industry and oversees the administration of the Texas workers’ compensation system. This data set includes counts for confirmed complaints and policies in force by company name and line of coverage. The complaint index is calculated by dividing the company's percentage of complaints for a specific line of insurance by the company's percentage of policies in force for the same line of insurance. The average index is 1.00. A number less than 1 indicates fewer complaints than average. A number greater than 1 indicates more complaints than average. rate_filings.name: Home and auto rate filings
rate_filings.description: This data set includes home and auto rate filings submitted by insurance companies to the Texas Department of Insurance. Click here to learn more about this data and the rate filing process.

columns.name: Company Name
columns.desc: Look at your insurance policy or billing statement or call your agent to ask the exact name of your company. You want to know the name of your company and not just the company group.

columns.name: Received Date
columns.desc: This is the date the filing was submitted to TDI.

columns.name: Type of Insurance
columns.desc: Personal auto or homeowners

columns.name: SubType of Insurance
columns.desc: This could further narrow the type of policies covered by the filing, such as for mobile owners, renters, or motorcycles.

columns.name: Product Name
columns.desc: Insurance companies sell products through agents and agencies. When filing rates, companies give product names to their filings. The product name can help you find the rate filing for your policy.   Your policy or billing statement should show the name of the policy sold to you. It may also include the name of the agent or agency that sold you the policy.

columns.name: Percent Change
columns.desc: This is the estimated overall impact that the rate change has on existing policyholders. Impacts could be higher or lower for any policyholder depending on changes to specific factors and the changing characteristics of the policyholder. If the Percent Change is blank or 0%, it could mean that only rules or other non-premium bearing items were changed in the filing or that the overall impact is 0%

columns.name: SERFF ID #
columns.desc: This is the filing number for the rate filing.

columns.name: Effective Date (new business)
columns.desc: This is the date when the rate starts getting charged for any new business written by the insurance company.

columns.name: Effective Date (renewal business)
columns.desc: This is the date when the rate starts getting charged for any existing business written by the insurance company.

columns.name: Status
columns.desc: A filing can be pending (still under review) or closed (review completed).

columns.name: Closed Type
columns.desc: This indicates the disposition of the filing.
